queue.arrival_note: No boot command is set. Set one now: run_command(node: "relh-sugarscape-baseline-recovery-cpu8-20261019-v1", command: "...", detach: true, on_wake: true, max_duration_minutes: N). It starts the moment the node is ready, even when you are not polling. Otherwise poll get_node and send a run_command inside the idle window (rate.minimum_minutes). A ready node with no command bills that window and then stops. Once the node runs, hold_node keeps it awake between your turns. Do not delete and re-create this node. The new node waits from zero. The delete also withdraws the demand that starts the next machine.
queue.demand_note: QUEUE DEPTH STARTS MORE MACHINES. Your queued node's GPUs are a term in the fleet's own demand target, counted on the next procurement pass, so joining this queue is what makes the fleet grow and withdrawing makes it shrink. A full fleet is a reason to queue, not a reason to hold work back - queued time is free, your place is held to expires_at, and holding the work back is the one move that guarantees no machine is ever started for it. This is not a promise of a machine (a spend ceiling or a frozen market still binds, and capacity_inbound says whether one is coming for THIS entry) - it is the direction: a queue nobody joins starts nothing.

queue.hold_note: this queue spot expires in 29m but the shape's own estimate to ready is 1h 13m (p90 7h 19m) - the hold lapses before the node can arrive. Extend it now with create_node(name: "relh-sugarscape-baseline-recovery-cpu8-20261019-v1", chip: "cpu-8", max_wait: "...") - the same name extends the live hold rather than creating a second node, forward-only, 12h ceiling - or pass max_wait up front on the call that queues it. A lapsed spot re-queued within 15 min keeps the place it waited for; after a lapse get_node reports status "expired" for an hour.
